parsed.explanation: The write-up's Part B only derives, by pigeonhole on 2^{n+1} signed sums, a nonzero delta in {-1,0,1}^{n+1} with |sum delta_i a_i| <= T_n S, and then states outright that such a signed sum is not always realizable by Xiang's operations ('Realizability gap'). The missing ingredient is exactly L3.2's construction: mirrored cuts pairing subset S against T and bisecting the rest, which realizes |Sigma(S)-Sigma(T)| with at most n cuts. Nowhere else in the text is this supplied; the status line says 'Part B (XY always forces D<=T_n) still open', with the only candidate described as empirical and needing proof. Hence the universal upper bound is not established as written; a full lemma is required.
